A also states that the deposit is readily convertible and subject to insignificant value risk. The question asks which investment can qualify under the maturity test, not for a maturity exactly at the three-month boundary.

An investment normally qualifies as cash equivalents only when it has a short maturity, of say, three months or less from the date of acquisition.

A_clauses.clause: , readily convertible with insignificant value risk
A_clauses.decisive_context: The option states ready convertibility and insignificant value risk, matching the relevant characteristics in the cash-equivalent definition.
premises: , readily convertible with insignificant value risk
Cash equivalents’ means short-term highly liquid investments that are readily convertible into known amounts of cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value.

A_clauses.clause: A short-term deposit acquired today and maturing in two months, readily convertible with insignificant value risk
A_clauses.decisive_context: Qualification as a cash equivalent under the maturity test and risk/convertibility criteria.

reviewed_terminal_controls.independent_diagnosis: The native outputs both choose A and both native source_support flags are true. OpenAI A clause 1 uses the exact option text as the two-month arithmetic input plus an exact excerpt for the three-month rule; the original resolver cannot bind options as arithmetic inputs. Gemini uses the exact excerpt premise, but its decisive_context is a generalized label rather than repeating that premise. Source absence about B redemption date cannot alone contradict B, so a semantic audit must leave that challenger unresolved unless additional support exists.

reviewed_terminal_controls.subject: accountancy

failure_details: NCERT classifies cash receipts from sale of goods as operating (E2.1); for a garment maker, garment sales are a principal revenue-generating activity (E1.1). On the ordinary reading that an old cutting machine is equipment being disposed of, its sale proceeds are investing (E3.1). Thus B is correct.
The two receipts are individually classified; no numerical calculation is required. The financing description concerns long-term funds or capital, not the stated customer payment for garments (E4.1).

A_clauses.decisive_context: The customer payment fits operating activities, but the ordinary reading of proceeds from selling an old cutting machine is disposal of equipment; proceeds from fixed-asset disposal are investing.
premises: payment from customers for delivered garments
cash receipts from sale of goods
Cash receipt from disposal of fixed assets.

A_clauses.decisive_context: Classification of proceeds from selling an old cutting machine
premises: Cash Inflows from Investing Activities include cash receipt from disposal of fixed assets including intangibles.

reviewed_terminal_controls.independent_diagnosis: Both choose B and both native source_support flags are true. OpenAI A clause cites exact stem facts (“payment from customers for delivered garments”; “selling an old cutting machine”) and source examples; Gemini cites the exact fixed-asset disposal rule. In both, decisive_context does not echo the exact source premise, which triggers the frozen first-clause check. Separately, “old cutting machine” is not an explicit stem assertion that the item is a fixed asset; retain that as a semantic ambiguity for independent audit instead of letting structural citation repair resolve it.

reviewed_terminal_controls.subject: accountancy

failure_details: The stem states that cash is paid to acquire a van for use over several years. The source explicitly lists cash payments to acquire fixed assets under cash outflows from investing activities (E5.1; also E1.1), so B is the supported classification.

Using the van in delivery operations does not change the classification of its acquisition; financing concerns long-term funds or capital (E3.1), and the source explicitly includes fixed-asset purchases as investing outflows (E5.1). The fixed-asset payment is not excluded.
This is an original-practice item. The authenticated CUET 2024 accountancy exemplar q25 was used only as a format/demand comparator, not as a source for the accounting rule.

A_clauses.decisive_context: The stem describes a cash payment to acquire a van for use over several years; E5.1 classifies cash payments to acquire fixed assets as investing outflows.
premises: A company pays cash to acquire a delivery van for use over several years.
Cash payments to acquire fixed assets including intangibles and capitalised research and development.

A_clauses.decisive_context: Classification of cash payment to acquire a fixed asset (delivery van).
premises: Cash payments to acquire fixed assets are cash outflows from investing activities.
Operating activities are principal revenue generating activities and are not investing or financing activities.

reviewed_terminal_controls.independent_diagnosis: Both choose B and both native source_support flags are true. OpenAI decomposes its reasoning into exact stem details plus the source heading/quoted fixed-asset payment rule. Gemini instead says “Cash payments to acquire fixed assets are cash outflows from investing activities.” This is not present as that sentence in the cited source; it is an inferred paraphrase from heading plus example and must remain unbound under the proposal. A real selected excerpt and a semantically plausible paraphrase do not establish an exact premise.
